content.title: South Carolina upsets UConn, ends 54-game win streak to advance to championship
content.text: April 3, 2026Updated April 4, 2026, 12:38 a.m. ETPHOENIX — There will be a new national champion.The defending national champion UConn women’s basketball team had its 54-game winning streak snapped, 62-48, by South Carolina in the semifinals at the Final Four on Friday night at Mortgage Matchup Arena.The Gamecocks, who lost to the Huskies in last year's title game, will try to capture their fourth national championship under coach Dawn Staley against the winner of the Texas-UCLA game.With 0.1 seconds left in the game, Auriemma and Staley got into at halfcourt, with Staley telling Auriemma, "Don't do that!" repeatedly. After the game, Staley walked over to the UConn bench with her hands up while Auriemma stormed off the court without shaking hands despite doing so before their altercation."I have no idea, but I'm going to let you know this, I'm of integrity. I'm of integrity," Staley said on the broadcast. "So if I did something wrong to Geno, I had no idea what I did, I guess he thought I didn't shake his hand at the beginning of the game, I didn't know, I went down there pregame, shook everybody on his staff's hand, I don't know what we came with after the game, but hey sometimes things get heated. We move on."It's possible Auriemma was upset about the disparity in fouls. UConn had 17 fouls compared to eight for South Carolina. The Gamecocks were 18-for-22 from the free throw line. The Huskies were 4-for-6.When asked what the exchange was about postgame, Auriemma said: "Nothing… I said what I had to say. Nothing. Nothing.” Staley said: “You can ask Geno the question… he’s the one who initiated the concession… I don’t want what happened there to dampen what we did in the game.”South Carolina held Sarah Strong and Azzi Fudd, the heartbeat of the UConn offense, to 20 points combined on 7-of-31 shooting. Strong added 12 rebounds, three steals and two blocks. Ashlynn Shade had 10 points.Strong was so frustrated, she ripped her jersey: “It was an accident. Missed my shot. Ripped it by accident.” She had to shed her No. 21 after she tore it and put on No. 55.Ta'Niya Latson, who transferred from Florida State to win a title, led the Gamecocks with a double-double. She had 16 points and 11 rebounds. Agot Makeer had 14 points and Joyce Edwards added 11 points and eight rebounds."(Dawn Staley) instilled belief in us." Latson said. "That was like the topic of ... the whole game. I mean, just the belief. Believe and to have confidence. I mean, we had to go out there and play South Carolina basketball, and I think we did that. Coach gave us, you know, the confidence and she has still belief in us. So I feel like we all played like that today."Staley didn't want to get bogged down in Auriemma's outburst."I'm super proud of our kids. I'm not going to let any incident take anything away from the performance on the floor," Staley said. Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley have wordsIt's unclear what UConn coach Geno Auriemma was upset about but he got in South Carolina coach Dawn Staley's face with less the a second to go. South Carolina upset?With 3:30 to go the Gamecocks lead by six, 53-47. Sarah Strong now wearing 55The sophomore's jersey ripped and she had to put on a new one. It's unclear if Strong's jersey was ripped and she finished the job or if she ripped it out of frustration. Geno Auriemma rips refsUConn coach Geno Auriemma went off during a TV timeout."There were six fouls called that quarter. All of them against us. They've been beating the [expletive] out of our guys down there the entire game. Now I'm not making excuses because we haven't been able to make a shot, but this is ridiculous."Their coach (Staley) rants and raves on the sideline, and calls the referee some names you don't wanna hear. And now we get ... Come on man. This is for the national championship."Read more here End of Q3: South Carolina 44, UConn 39The Huskies have not trailed at the end of the third quarter this season, until now. The Gamecocks are outrebounding UConn 35-25 and outscoring them in the paint 26-20.Joyce Edwards, Ta'Niya Latson and Tessa Johnson have 10 points each for South Carolina. Latson, a transfer from Florida State also has nine rebounds.Ashlynn Shade lead UConn with 10 points. Sarah Strong has been held to eight points on 3-of-13 shooting. UConn hits back-to-back-to-back 3sKayleigh Heckel, Blanca Quiñonez and Azzi Fudd hit 3-points to cut the Gamecoack's lead — which had ballooned to 10 points — to one 40-39.KK Arnold sheds the maskThe Huskies junior point guard came out after halftime without her black mask over her face. KK Arnold began wearing a protective face mask in early January 2026 after suffering a nasal fracture in late December. She missed one game, a New Year's Eve matchup against Providence. South Carolina takes eight-point lead to open halfThe Gamecocks have eight points from four different players and have jumped out to their largest lead of the game. The Huskies have yet to score in 4:35. South Carolina has its largest lead of the game. Halftime: UConn 26, South Carolina 24The game could not be more even through one half as both teams have 18 points in the paint and have hit one 3-pointer each.The Huskies have slightly better shooting percentage at 40% to the Gamecocks 31%. South Carolina is outrebounding UConn, 24-16.Sarah Strong has eight points, six rebounds, two steals and two blocks for UConn. Ashlynn Shade added eight points.Joyce Edwards, Ta'Niya Latson and Tessa Johnson have six points each for South Carolina. Joyce Edwards sets single season record for scoringJoyce Edwards passed Katrina Anderson for the South Carolina women's basketball single-season scoring record. Anderson had with 754 points in the 1977-78 season. Azzi Fudd help Huskies take lead backUConn takes the lead back, 24-23, on Azzi's Fudd defensive rebound and 12-foot floater in transition. The Huskies trailed by as many as five in the quarter. Diana Taurasi, Paige Bueckers in attendanceThe Women’s Final Four matchup between UConn and South Carolina is a star-studded affair. Famous alumni, including UConn legends Diana Taurasi, Maya Moore and Paige Bueckers, in addition to South Carolina alum Aliyah Boston, were spotted in Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. Here’s a running list of all the celebs in attendance. South Carolina takes the leadThe Gamecocks took their first lead since the opening minute on a Ta'Niya Latson layup. South Carolina lead 17-15. End of 1Q: South Carolina 15, UConn 15South Carolina's Agot Makeer hit a 3-pointer as time expired in the first quarter to tie it up. UConn led by as many as seven early but had trouble with turnovers and shooting in the waning minutes.Sarah Strong has five points and Serah Williams and Ashlynn Shade four each for the Huskies. Blanca Quiñonez has two fouls.Tessa Johnson and Ta'Niya Latson have four points each for the Gamecocks. Sarah Strong getting hotThe sophomore sensation has five points a rebound and a steal as UConn is out to a 13-8 lead. Strong won every player of the year award this week and is looking to lead the Huskies to back-to-back national titles. We are under way in PhoenixSerah Williams has four points for UConn and Ta'Niya Latson four for South Carolina. Williams transferred to the Huskies from Wisconsin and Latson to the Gamecocks from Florida State.
